keyVocab: Categorical variable: describes a quality or category, not a quantity
Nominal: categories with no natural order (e.g. eye colour)
Ordinal: categories with a natural order (e.g. shirt size)
Numerical variable: values are quantities
Discrete: counted, whole-number values
Continuous: measured, any value in a range
Frequency table: lists each value and how often it occurs (count and %)
Bar chart: a bar for each category, bars separated by gaps
Segmented bar chart: one bar split into segments, one per category
Mode (modal category): the most common value or category

Standard deviation (s): spread of the data around the mean

keyVocab: Bivariate data: two variables recorded for each individual
Explanatory variable (EV): the variable that may explain or predict changes in the other variable
Response variable (RV): the variable that responds to changes in the EV

Percentaged two-way table: percentages calculated within each category of the EV
Association: knowing the value of one variable helps predict the value of the other
Segmented bar chart: one bar per EV category, split by the RV
